key: e:eu type-approval regime for automated driving systems
synopsis: The skeptic’s review identifies the EU automated-driving type-approval regime as the most simulation-friendly regulator found, while emphasizing that simulation cannot substitute for its physical tests [f10410, f11161]. The regime requires a documented credibility assessment defining the envelope within which a virtual toolchain may be used [f10411, f14951]. The glossary adds that each model must have documented validation, and both locations require evidence of the competence of teams validating and using the toolchain [f14951, f10412]. These facts concern an on-road regime; they do not establish its applicability to heavy off-road machines [f10410, f14951].

relations.note: Both state that simulation cannot substitute for physical tests.
Glossary repeats the validity-envelope requirement and adds model validation and team competence.
Glossary repeats team competence requirements and adds credibility assessment and model validation.
